summary.text: Kris Kobach is the Republican Attorney General of Kansas and lost re-election on November 3, 2026 to Chris Mann.
He served as Kansas Secretary of State from 2011 to 2019 and has been Attorney General since 2023.

paragraphs.text: Kobach was raised in Topeka and graduated from Washburn Rural High School.

He graduated from Harvard University in government, first in his department and summa cum laude, received a Ph.D. in politics from the University of Oxford as a Marshall Scholar, and earned a J.D. from Yale Law School.
He clerked for the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals and then became a professor of constitutional law at the University of Missouri–Kansas City School of Law.
He was a White House Fellow under President George W. Bush and served in the U.S. Department of Justice as Counsel to Attorney General John Ashcroft.
Kobach was the 31st Kansas Secretary of State, serving from 2011 to 2019.
He ran for governor in 2018 and lost to Laura Kelly.

Before becoming attorney general, he brought three federal lawsuits against the Biden administration: over vaccine mandates, over limits on immigration detention and deportation by ICE agents and sheriffs, and over the Air Force's expulsion of pilots at McConnell Air Force Base.
Kobach became the state's 45th Attorney General in 2023, and in October 2024 he was affirmed as chairman of the Republican Attorneys General Association.
He lives near Lecompton with his wife, Heather, and their five children.
During the campaign, his emphasis was on lower crime rates, a fentanyl task force, and lawsuits against federal policy.
He received 49.4% of the vote to Chris Mann's 50.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News and HPPR / KCUR, and the Associated Press called the race for Mann.
